findings.Description: Express framework default X-Powered-By header can expose underlying server technology stack.
findings.Evidence: Server responses omit X-Powered-By via helmet({ hidePoweredBy: true }).
findings.ExploitationScenario: An attacker scans response headers to fingerprint Express and search for framework-specific zero-days.
findings.Impact: Negligible in current state due to active Helmet suppression.
findings.Remediation: Ensure app.disable("x-powered-by") or helmet() remains top-level middleware.
findings.VerificationSteps: Execute curl -I against /api/health and confirm X-Powered-By header is absent.

findings.Description: Weak passwords could make user accounts susceptible to offline dictionary or credential stuffing attacks.
findings.Evidence: Registration route enforces regex: min 8 chars, 1 uppercase, 1 lowercase, 1 number.
findings.ExploitationScenario: Users attempt registering trivial passwords like "123456" or "password".
findings.Impact: Eliminated: registration controller returns HTTP 400 with password strength guidance.
findings.Remediation: Maintain server-side validatePasswordStrength() validation before calling user creation.
findings.VerificationSteps: POST /api/auth/register with password "weak" and confirm 400 rejection.

findings.Description: Raw bank account numbers displayed to frontend clients pose visual and network privacy risks.
findings.Evidence: API masks account numbers (e.g. *******7890) before returning payload to the client.
findings.ExploitationScenario: Unauthorized shoulder surfing or API interception reveals full financial account numbers.
findings.Impact: Mitigated: full account numbers are stored securely and never transmitted unmasked.
findings.Remediation: Keep server-side masking in the getter pipeline.
findings.VerificationSteps: GET /api/owner/bank-details and verify accountNumber contains masking asterisks.
